title: Codec Latent-Space Map
description: A per-latent-space dialect for the Codec v0.3 latent modality. Carries the data needed to negotiate latent transport (shape, dtype, vae_scale_factor, accepted pipelines), to identify a paired VAE decoder, and to compress latent streams (per-pipeline zstd dictionaries). Latent-space maps are content-addressed and immutable: a new VAE version publishes a new map at a new URL with a new sha256 hash. Symmetric to spec/tokenizer-map.schema.json for the v0.2 text modality.

id.description: Stable, globally unique latent-space identifier. Convention: lowercase 'org/vae-family' matching the upstream weights repo, e.g. 'stabilityai/sd-vae-ft-mse', 'stabilityai/sdxl-vae', 'stabilityai/wan-vae-2.1'. Same ID + same hash means byte-identical map. Used as `LatentStreamHeader.latent_space_id` on the wire.

version.description: Schema version. '1' for the current schema (v0.3 launch). Implementations SHOULD reject maps whose version they don't recognize rather than silently degrading.

shape.description: Per-frame latent tensor shape, channel-first. For SD-1 / SD-2 family: [4, 64, 64] at 512×512; for SDXL: [4, 128, 128] at 1024×1024; for video VAEs: [C, T, H, W] or [C, H, W] depending on whether T is per-frame or per-stream. The first axis MUST be the channel axis (Codec pipelines quantize per-channel).

dtype.description: Native dtype of latents emitted by the canonical decoder pre-pipeline. The `raw` pipeline ships these bytes verbatim; quantizing pipelines (`int8`, `int4`, etc.) accept fp16/bf16/fp32 inputs and emit int8/int4 on the wire: the wire dtype is then implied by the `pipeline` field on `LatentStreamHeader`, not by this `dtype`. Servers MUST cast inbound latents to this dtype before any pipeline runs.

vae_scale_factor.description: The model's published latent-to-pixel scale (e.g. 0.18215 for SD-1.5 / SD-2, 0.13025 for SDXL). Decoders multiply latents by this constant before VAE inference; the value is informational on the wire (clients with a cached decoder don't need it), but it travels in `LatentStreamHeader.vae_scale_factor` so a thin client can stand up a new decoder without out-of-band lookup.

pipelines.description: Closed list of byte-level transport pipelines the server is willing to emit for this latent space. The pipeline name appears verbatim in `LatentStreamHeader.pipeline` and MUST be one of the registered names below. A client requesting a pipeline absent from this list MUST receive a 4xx response: servers MUST NOT silently downgrade. Adding a pipeline is a v0.3+ point release; per-deployment extension is not supported. Each entry's quality_thresholds[] is the contract pixels-after-decode must meet (LPIPS / SSIM / PSNR vs the frozen reference).

name.description: Pipeline identifier. See spec/PIPELINES.md for the full forward/inverse math per name. `raw` is bit-exact and is the only pipeline mandatory for every latent-space map. Quantizing pipelines (`int8`, `int4`) require `static_scales` (per-channel fp16 array: see `static_scales` below). Adaptive variants compute scales per keyframe and prepend them to the frame. Delta variants are video-only and require keyframe cadence.

static_scales.description: Required for pipelines `int8` and `int4` (the static-scale variants). Carries the per-channel symmetric quantization scales the server uses every frame. Same scales used by every client that decodes against this map: the encoder/decoder agreement is what makes the round-trip bit-exact at the latent-byte boundary.

url.description: URL of the per-channel scales file. Body is C × 2 raw little-endian fp16 bytes (no header), where C is shape[0]. Same wire layout as `LatentStreamHeader.scales`.

hash.description: sha256 of the scales file body, prefixed with 'sha256:'. Implementations MUST verify before loading.

size_bytes.description: Size of the scales file in bytes; equals 2 × shape[0]. Informational.

keyframe_interval_frames.description: Required for delta pipelines (video). Maximum number of frames between keyframes; the server MUST emit a `LatentFrame` with `keyframe=true` at least this often, and the client uses it to bound its delta-decode buffer. Image-latent pipelines ignore this field.

quality_thresholds.description: Perceptual quality bounds the pipeline guarantees against the frozen reference decoder for this latent space (typically pinned-torch + diffusers in a content-addressed Docker image: see decoder.canonical_image). Reported by `latents validate` and gated by `@codecai/maps-cli` before a map can ship. Absent on `raw` (which is bit-exact pre-decoder; only the decoder's own non-determinism applies).

ssim_min.description: Minimum SSIM vs reference decoded pixels, averaged over the fixture suite.

psnr_min_db.description: Minimum PSNR in dB vs reference.

lpips_max.description: Maximum LPIPS distance vs reference. Lower is better; values >0.2 are typically perceptible.

fixture_suite.description: Identifier of the fixture suite these thresholds were measured against (e.g. 'sd-vae-ft-mse-512-v1'). Lives under packages/bench/golden/.

decoder.description: Optional canonical decoder reference. A Codec-aware client that wants to render pixels (rather than only ferry latents to a downstream model) uses this block to load a paired VAE. The wire is fully decoder-free without it: gateways and inference engines never need this field.

family.description: Decoder runtime family. `torch` is the canonical reference; `onnx` / `ggml` / `wgsl` are alternative runtimes that meet the same `quality_thresholds`. Multiple families MAY be advertised by repeating this block under per-family URLs in client-side config: the schema captures one canonical entry.

model_class.description: Class name within the decoder family, e.g. 'AutoencoderKL' for diffusers, 'AutoencoderKLWan' for Wan-VAE, or an ONNX graph identifier. Combined with `weights_url` this is enough to load the decoder.

weights_url.description: Optional URL the decoder weights can be fetched from. Often a HuggingFace mirror. Absent when the decoder is bundled with the runtime (e.g. ggml model files distributed separately).

weights_hash.description: sha256 of the decoder weights file. Required if `weights_url` is set.

canonical_image.description: Docker image (registry/name@sha256:...) that produced the perceptual reference pixels the `quality_thresholds` were measured against. The bench's `golden-builder` produces this image. Pinning at the image-digest level means the reference is reproducible across machines.

zstd_dictionaries.description: Optional pre-trained ZSTD dictionaries for compressing latent streams. UNLIKE the v0.2 text-side dicts (keyed only by wire format), latent dicts are keyed by `(format, pipeline)`: the byte distribution of int8 latents is wildly different from raw fp16 or delta+int4 residuals. A dict trained against one pipeline is meaningless against another as a result. A server MUST NOT respond with `Content-Encoding: zstd` unless it has loaded a dict whose `(format, pipeline)` matches the response. The active dict's sha256 travels in the `Codec-Zstd-Dict` response header. See PROTOCOL.md §'Compression and dictionaries' (Latent Modality section).

format.description: Codec wire format this dictionary was trained against.

pipeline.description: Pipeline whose post-pipeline byte stream this dictionary was trained on. MUST appear in the parent `pipelines[]` list.

url.description: URL the dictionary file can be fetched from. Body MUST be raw zstd dictionary bytes (output of `zstd --train` or `zstandard.train_dictionary`), not a JSON wrapper.

hash.description: sha256 of the dictionary file body, prefixed with 'sha256:'. Implementations MUST verify before loading.

size_bytes.description: Size of the dictionary file in bytes. Informational.

trained_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this dictionary was trained. Informational.

corpus_summary.description: Free-form metadata about the training corpus (sample count, prompt-shape mix, fixture-suite reference). Useful for downstream auditors deciding whether to re-train.

published_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this map was published. Informational only: content addressing is via sha256 hash.
